title: Non-Movement Symptoms
content: Parkinson's disease can cause many symptoms that are unrelated to movement. These non-movement symptoms can significantly affect everyday life and, for some people, can be more troublesome than movement symptoms. They can include depression, anxiety, apathy, cognitive changes, sleep problems, daytime fatigue, constipation, bladder problems, pain, speech or swallowing difficulties, dizziness and other changes. Symptoms vary substantially between individuals, so a person with Parkinson's will not necessarily experience all of these problems.
